title: Separate acquired algebra from tractable critical geometry
statement: H=X1(X2X3+X4X5) has radical-free third form and full scalar chain centroid, yet its projective singular locus contains a positive-dimensional quadric and an isolated vertex. Over F8 it has82 points,81 with degenerate transverse Hessian. Centroid acquisition alone does not supply the contact counting gates.

requires: The actual rank-five witness over the source's characteristic-two field/chain setting
Keep the residue projective critical geometry separate from the scalar centroid
provides: A concrete counterexample to scalar-centroid/radical-free implying finitely many nondegenerate critical rays
assumptions: The source raw example uses F8[t]/t^2; the displayed residue geometry is explicit
This particular witness is not claimed #P-hard
costs: Actual critical-locus acquisition and its size must be charged
The contact counter correctly rejects its singular M gate
contract.units: Original independent Boolean bits; F_(2^d) elements and ordinary field/ring exponents are distinct from Boolean ANF masks. Exact signed/zero counts and source-local phase/rank/depth units.
contract.obstruction: No generic higher-module-rank evaluator follows merely from recovering the algebra. The missing geometry is a real extra hypothesis.

body: The singular locus consists of X1=0, X2X3+X4X5=0, plus[1:0:0:0:0]. It has(q+1)^2+1 field points. The same source proves the scalar centroid explicitly and preserves a raw six-dimensional-centroid acquisition. The example fails the contact square-matrix nonsingularity gate, rather than contradicting a theorem with that gate.

evidence.quote: ## 5. Decisive geometric obstruction to a generic higher-b counter
evidence.range_scope: Actual radical-free full-centroid counterexample and projective critical-locus calculation, not a hardness claim for this witness.

review.scope: Completed archived general-module audit's explicit counterexample proof; no generic counting or numerical replay inferred.
